body.heading: Think of someone
paragraphs: Think of a person who helped you, taught you something, or made you smile. Talk about them with your adult.
Fold a piece of card or thick paper in half. This will be your kindness card.

body.heading: Make the card
paragraphs: Draw a picture on the front. It can be anything cheerful: a sun, a flower, a rainbow, or the person's favourite animal.
Inside, write or dictate a short message. Try: “Thank you for helping me.” Your adult can help with tricky words. A short message from the heart is perfect.

body.heading: Give it away
paragraphs: Give the card to the person with your adult nearby, or ask your adult to help you deliver it safely.
You do not need to wait for a special day. A surprise card on an ordinary day can feel extra special.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: make simple cards that say thank you, well done, or I am thinking of you.

safetyNotes: Only give cards to people you and your adult know, and let your adult help with any delivering.
Do not write your home address or other private details on the card.
screenFreeExtension: Make a second card for someone in your own home and hide it somewhere kind, like under a pillow or in a lunchbox.
takeaway: A handmade card is a small way to tell someone they matter.
